item.title: Nigerian teenager jailed for defrauding American man of $800
item.description: The Federal High Court sitting in Ikoyi, Lagos, has convicted and sentenced an 18-year-old man, Hassan Usman Olamilekan, for money laundering involving $800 obtained through a lottery scam. Justice Dipeolu delivered the judgment on October 30, 2026, following Olamilekan’s arraignment by the Lagos Zonal Directorate 1 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). Olamilekan was arraigned on a one-count charge of money laundering, contrary to Section 18(2)(a) and punishable under Section 18(3) of the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022. The defendant pleaded guilty to the charge, after which an EFCC operative, Ebuka Abanga, reviewed the facts of the case before the court found him guilty. Justice Dipeolu sentenced him to a fine of N200,000 and ordered him to pay N1 million in restitution to the Federal Government. The court further ordered that he remains in the correctional centre pending payment of the fine and restitution. It also ordered the forfeiture of an iPhone 11 Pro and a Poco C71 mobile phone recovered in connection with the offence. According to the EFCC, investigations revealed that Olamilekan, who claimed to be from the Republic of Benin but was born in Nigeria, operated several social media platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Zangi and iMessage, which he allegedly used for internet fraud. The commission said he met his victim, an American citizen identified as Gary Brewer, through the Zangi application, where he impersonated a white American woman named Julie Leach. Olamilekan reportedly told Brewer that he had won a $250 million lottery prize but needed money to activate the winnings before he could claim the funds. He subsequently persuaded the victim to send him gift cards through the messaging platform. The EFCC said the defendant admitted selling the gift cards through the Cardsonic application, converting the proceeds into naira and transferring the money to his grandmother’s OPay account. He also confessed to benefiting $800 from the fraudulent scheme. Olamilekan was among 21 suspected internet fraudsters arrested by EFCC operatives during a sting operation at Applewood Estate, Orchid Road, Lekki, Lagos State, on October 26, 2026. item.title: Reps move to reform 69-year-old Trustee Investment Act
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has begun moves to reform Nigeria’s 69-year-old Trustee Investments Act, while seeking a coordinated regulatory framework to tackle fraud, fragmented property records and weak consumer protection in the real estate sector. Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, said the proposed reforms were aimed at modernising the country’s legal framework to reflect changing financial and investment realities, while protecting the interests of beneficiaries and investors. Abbas, represented by a member of the House representing Lafia/Obi Federal Constituency, Nasarawa State, Dahiru Abubakar Sarki, spoke on Monday at a public hearing on the Trustee Investment Act (Repeal and Enactment) Bill, 2026, at the National Assembly, Abuja. The bill, sponsored by Solomon Bob, seeks to repeal and replace the existing Trustee Investments Act of 1957, which Abbas described as outdated in the face of developments in Nigeria’s capital market and emerging investment opportunities. He said the existing law was enacted in a substantially different economic and financial environment, noting that the investment landscape had changed considerably over the past seven decades. According to him, capital markets have expanded, financial instruments have become more sophisticated, and new opportunities for investment and wealth creation have emerged, making legislative reform necessary. “The challenge is to strike the right balance between preserving trust assets and enabling reasonable returns on investment. “An excessively restrictive framework may deny beneficiaries legitimate opportunities for growth, while an inadequately regulated one may expose their assets to imprudent decisions and avoidable risks,” he said. Abbas stressed that expanded investment opportunities under the proposed legislation must be accompanied by strong safeguards, clear fiduciary responsibilities, effective risk management and appropriate regulatory oversight. He said trustees must be guided by prudence, integrity and transparency, adding that assets held in trust must be managed in the interests of beneficiaries rather than for the personal advantage of trustees. The Speaker said a credible framework for managing trust investments could contribute to deeper capital markets and more effective mobilisation of domestic resources to support infrastructure development and economic growth. He urged stakeholders to pay particular attention to investment categories, diversification requirements, fiduciary obligations, professional delegation and regulatory oversight in considering the bill. Seeks coordinated real estate regulation In a related development, Abbas has called for a coordinated national real estate regulatory system to tackle property fraud, eliminate institutional overlaps and strengthen investor confidence in Nigeria’s housing market. He made the call in a keynote address at a stakeholders’ conference on the proposed National Real Estate Regulator

item.title: 2027: My government will create 20 Dangotes in four years — Adebayo
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has promised that, if elected to office in 2027, his government would create “even 20 Dangotes” in four years by supporting refineries and boosting exports. Adebayo made the pledge during a recent interview on Nigeria Info’s Road to 2027 programme, while outlining how he would lower petrol prices without undermining private refinery investment. “Our government in four years will create even 20 Dangotes for exports; that is why God gave Nigeria a refinery by the water side,” he said, explaining that his plan would support refineries that export products and earn foreign exchange for Nigeria. He also said his administration would offer refineries long-term tax rebates and regulatory certainty, and give them 90 days to pay for government-supplied crude oil. “When I sell crude to you, I give you 90 days to pay. That is twice your throughput. You will have refined the crude, ship it overseas, collect the dollar, then you pay me,” he said. Adebayo added that refineries exporting their products would earn foreign exchange for Nigeria, while the government would ensure domestic consumers were not charged international prices. “If your refinery is for the international market, I will support you domestically, but you will be exporting and earning foreign exchange for us,” he said. “But you are not going to sell petrol at international prices to a teacher who does not earn an international salary.” He also said Nigeria’s four government-owned refineries would operate and that private refineries could receive domestic crude to serve the local market. “So, what we are saying is that for our own domestic markets, we have our own four refineries; they are going to work. Secondly, if you, a private refinery, want to participate, we will give you the crude at zero cost because it is domestic crude,” he added. item.title: Troops destroy kidnappers’ hideout in Kogi, recover ammunition
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army have destroyed a suspected kidnappers’ hideout in Edimogbo Forest, Igalamela/Odolu Local Government Area of Kogi State, recovering 1,000 rounds of ammunition, six motorcycles and other items. The operation was carried out by troops of the 21 Battalion Quick Reaction Force following intelligence reports indicating the presence of suspected kidnappers in the forest. The Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Col. Appolonia Anele, disclosed this in a statement on Monday. She said the troops mobilised to locate the suspected criminals after receiving credible human intelligence about their activities. “On approaching the hideout, the suspected kidnappers, on sighting the advancing troops, fired a shot to alert other members of the group before fleeing deeper into the forest. “The troops immediately pursued the fleeing criminals deep into the forest, but no contact was made,” she said. Anele said the troops subsequently destroyed the camp, including its supporting structures. Items recovered from the hideout included 1,000 rounds of 7.62mm by 54 ammunition, seven bandoliers, two shovels, a hand pump, a mobile phone, a Glo modem, two packets of soap and a jerrycan of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS). Other items recovered were clothing, pairs of shoes and six daylong motorcycles. She said troops were still combing the surrounding area in a bid to track down the fleeing suspects. The Army, according to her, remains committed to sustaining offensive operations against kidnappers and other criminal elements threatening the safety and security of law-abiding citizens. It also urged members of the public to continue providing credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to dismantle criminal networks. item.title: Makinde’s administration hit by fresh resignation wave as three more appointees quit
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Government has been hit by a fresh wave of resignations following the departure of three political appointees, including a member of the Oyo State Independent Electoral Commission (OYSIEC), Sunday Olugbenga Falana; the Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, Ayobami Oluwaseun Ojo; and the Special Adviser to Governor Seyi Makinde on Budget and Economic Planning, Simeon Adegbola Oyeleke. The three officials tendered their resignations on Monday, with their decisions taking immediate effect, in what represents another significant development in the evolving political landscape of the state ahead of the 2027 general elections. Falana, an indigene of Ogbomoso, communicated his decision in a resignation letter dated November 2, addressed to Governor Makinde through the Chief of Staff. In the letter, the former OYSIEC member expressed gratitude to the governor for the opportunity to serve on the state’s electoral management body, describing his experience as worthwhile. He, however, offered no explanation for his decision to leave the commission. His resignation came shortly after Ojo formally relinquished his position as Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning in a letter addressed to the governor through the Secretary to the State Government. Ojo, who hails from Ago-Are in Atisbo Local Government Area, submitted his resignation on Monday, November 2, referencing his appointment letter dated June 22, 2026. The former commissioner thanked Makinde for the confidence reposed in him and the opportunity to serve in his administration, describing his appointment and experience in government as a great honour. He, however, did not disclose the circumstances surrounding his departure. Similarly, Oyeleke, who served as the governor’s Special Adviser on Budget and Economic Planning, also tendered his resignation on the same day. Unlike the other two officials, however, the former two-term member of the Oyo State House of Assembly and former local government chairman gave an indication of the circumstances behind his decision, citing dissatisfaction with the working environment within the administration. In his resignation letter, Oyeleke said he was no longer comfortable with the prevailing working environment, which he described as unconducive to effectively pursuing and fulfilling the aspirations of his people within the administration. Despite his decision to step down, he expressed appreciation to Governor Makinde for his leadership, encouragement and support, as well as the opportunity to contribute to the policies and developmental programmes of the government. The simultaneous departures of the three officials have further drawn attention to the latest developments within the Makinde administration, particularly against the backdrop of recent changes involving political appointees and government officials. item.title: Francis Duru’s family announces funeral arrangements
item.description: The family of late Nollywood actor Francis Duru has announced plans for his burial, with funeral activities scheduled to take place in Abuja and his hometown in Imo State. The arrangements were disclosed in a statement published on the actor’s official Instagram page on Monday and jointly signed by his sister, Anthonia Chenyi, and his first son, Ebuka Duru. According to the family, a service of songs will be held on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, at Family Worship Centre, Idris Gidado Street, Wuye, Abuja, beginning at 5pm. The statement also announced that a second service of songs would take place on Thursday, December 10, at the late Pa Theophilus Ogide Duru’s family compound in Okai, Eziama, Isiala Mbano, Imo State. The burial and interment will follow on Friday, December 11, at the same location. “Service of songs in Abuja on Wednesday, 25th November 2026 by 5:00 PM at Family Worship Center, Idris Gidado Street, Wuye. “Service of songs in Imo State on Thursday, 10th December 2026 at the late Pa Theophilus Ogide Duru’s Family Compound, Okai, Eziama, Isiala Mbano. Followed by funeral and interment on Friday. Recall Vanguard reported that the 59-year-old actor died October 22, 2026 , after his battle with an undisclosed illness. item.title: INEC chairman says AI can strengthen democracy, warns against election disinformation
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has said artificial intelligence can improve Nigeria’s electoral process, insisting that the technology should not be regarded as a threat to democracy despite the risks associated with its misuse. Amupitan made the remarks on Monday at The Beyond the Ballot Summit in Abuja, where he highlighted the potential of AI to improve voter registration, logistics planning, data analysis and the management of large voter databases. He said electoral management bodies across the world were increasingly adopting AI-assisted systems to improve administrative efficiency and strengthen election planning. “Artificial Intelligence, AI, is not an enemy of democracy,” the INEC chairman said. However, he warned that the growing accessibility of generative AI tools had made it easier for individuals to produce deceptive materials capable of influencing voters and damaging public confidence in elections. According to him, technologies that previously required significant technical expertise and resources can now be used to clone the voices of public figures and create realistic videos of election officials making false announcements. He warned that such developments could expose electoral processes to targeted manipulation, particularly during sensitive stages of an election. The remarks come as INEC prepares for the 2027 general election and considers integrating artificial intelligence into aspects of Nigeria’s electoral administration. Concerns over the technology have also emerged following the discovery of questionable photographs in INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters in Etsako West Local Government Area of Edo State. Some images in the voter records were suspected to have been generated using artificial intelligence, raising concerns about the accuracy of the registration database and the verification procedures used during voter enrolment. INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, reportedly linked some of the questionable images to alleged irregularities involving registration officers who had access to the commission’s system. The commission said the register was still preliminary and would undergo verification, data cleaning and corrections before the final version is certified. The development has brought renewed attention to the challenges electoral authorities may face as they introduce emerging technologies into election management. While AI could help INEC process information, improve administrative planning and manage electoral data, its misuse could also facilitate voter impersonation, fabricated election announcements and the circulation of misleading audio and video recordings. item.title: Bauchi LGA chairman dies in road Accident
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Chairman of Zaki Local Government Area of Bauchi State, Masud Aliyu Umar, has died in a road accident while returning from an Allied Peoples Movement (APM) stakeholders’ meeting in Bauchi. Umar reportedly died on Sunday night when his private car crashed at Konkiyal Village in Darazo Local Government Area, about 100 kilometres from Bauchi metropolis. He was said to be travelling back to Zaki after attending the political meeting when the accident occurred. Before his election as Zaki LGA chairman on August 17, 2026, Umar served as Director-General of the Bauchi State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA). Reacting to his death, Governor Bala Mohammed expressed shock, describing Umar as a dedicated public servant, committed grassroots politician and compassionate leader whose contributions to public service and community development would remain indelible in the state. In a condolence message issued by his media aide, Mukhtar Gidado, the governor said Umar’s tenure at SEMA was marked by his commitment to alleviating the suffering of vulnerable citizens and providing timely assistance to communities affected by emergencies and humanitarian challenges. Mohammed added that, as chairman of Zaki Local Government, Umar demonstrated commitment to grassroots development through initiatives aimed at empowering youths and women, improving livelihoods and promoting inclusive development. He described the death as a major loss to the deceased’s family, the people of Zaki and Bauchi State, particularly the public service and local government administration. The governor urged the family, political associates, friends and people of Zaki Local Government to draw strength and comfort from Almighty Allah during the difficult period. The funeral prayer is scheduled for 2pm on Monday, November 2, 2026, at the Palace of the District Head, Mur Mur, Zaki Local Government Area of Bauchi State. item.title: Aston Villa drop legal action threat against Jammie Carragher
item.description: Aston Villa have withdrawn their threat of legal action against former Liverpool defender and Sky Sports pundit, Jamie Carragher, following his public apology over remarks directed at the club and its supporters. The Premier League club had announced on Friday that it intended to take legal action against Carragher over what it described as “unacceptable insults about the club and its fans”. The controversy followed comments made by Carragher on the Stick to Football podcast, where he criticised Villa supporters over discussions surrounding the possibility of manager Unai Emery leaving the club for Manchester United. During the podcast, Carragher told Villa supporters to “shut the f*** up”, a remark that sparked anger among the club’s supporters and attracted criticism from within the club. However, according to The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender issued an apology on Saturday, describing his choice of words as “clumsy and wrong”. “I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners and their fans. My language this week was clumsy and wrong,” he said. He added that although his comments were intended as a joke, he understood why they had offended supporters. “I can assure Villa fans it was tongue in cheek, but I can understand it’s not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today, UTV [Up the Villa]!” Carragher stated. Following the apology, Aston Villa dropped its threat of legal action, bringing an end to the immediate dispute between the club and the television pundit. Carragher, who enjoyed a successful playing career at Liverpool before becoming a prominent football analyst, is also a columnist for The Telegraph. item.title: Police arrest man for allegedly pushing teenager from two-storey building in Imo
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — The Imo State Police Command has arrested a 26-year-old man, Ifeanyichukwu Joseph, for allegedly attempting to kill his girlfriend’s 17-year-old niece, Chiamaka Chukwuokorie, by pushing her from a two-storey building in Owerri. The incident reportedly occurred on November 1, 2026, at about 1pm, following an alleged altercation between the suspect and the teenager at Mbonu Ejike Street, Ikenegbu, Owerri. Confirming the incident in a statement, the Police Public Relations Officer, Henry Okoye, said the victim sustained serious injuries and was rushed to a nearby hospital, where she is receiving treatment in critical condition. Okoye said the suspect was rescued by police operatives after an angry mob reportedly attempted to lynch him following the incident. He said the suspect was subsequently taken into police custody and was being investigated to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and facilitate appropriate legal action. The police spokesman urged members of the public, particularly social media users, to refrain from circulating unverified information about the incident. He quoted the Commissioner of Police, Imo State Command, CP Audu Garba Bosso, as assuring residents that the incident was being thoroughly investigated and that all necessary steps would be taken to establish the facts and ensure justice. The commissioner also appealed to residents to remain calm, avoid taking the law into their hands and allow the police to carry out their duties professionally. The command said further developments would be communicated to the public as the investigation progresses. item.title: British adventurer completes 28-year, 50,000km walk home
item.description: A 57-year-old British adventurer, Karl Bushby, has returned home after completing a remarkable 28-year, 50,000-kilometre journey on foot across four continents without using any form of transport to advance his trek. Bushby arrived in his home city of Hull, northeast England, on Monday, where he was welcomed by a cheering crowd of up to 1,000 people after completing the extraordinary journey that began in Chile in 1998. The former British paratrooper, who embarked on the adventure at the age of 29, had two rules for the expedition: never use transport to move forward and never return home until he had completed the challenge. Addressing the crowd, Bushby thanked those who supported him throughout the journey, describing the achievement as a collective effort. “I didn’t do this alone,” he said, adding that it had been a “global effort”. He said the journey involved overcoming numerous obstacles, including challenges involving governments and difficult geographical conditions. “You wouldn’t believe just how many people have been involved in this, to get us around the kinds of obstacles that we face. We’ve faced down governments, we’ve faced down some of the hardest challenges,” he said. His route took him through the length of the Americas, across the frozen Bering Strait from Alaska into Russia, and through parts of Central Asia and Europe. Along the way, he traversed jungles, mountains and deserts, pushing his belongings on a metal-framed cart. He was applauded on Sunday as he crossed the iconic Humber Bridge near Hull in thick mist before making his final approach to the city centre. Hull Mayor, Maria Coward, who welcomed him on Monday, praised his determination and perseverance. “So many people have followed Karl on his epic journey. We have all felt inspired by his spirit, tenacity and dogged determination,” she said, describing the achievement as a source of pride for the city. Bushby was also expected to reunite with his mother, Angela, his 36-year-old son, Adam, and a 12-year-old granddaughter he had never met. He began the expedition following the breakdown of his marriage, after his wife returned to Northern Ireland with their son. His journey was interrupted several times, including when Russia refused to grant him a visa. The 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic also forced him to suspend the expedition. During the interruptions, he temporarily settled in different locations, including a base in Mexico, before resuming the trek from the exact point where he had stopped. In early October, he swam across the English Channel to return to the United Kingdom. “Feels good to have UK soil under my feet after all these years,” he said in a statement, acknowledging that the journey had not been easy. “All of us can accomplish more than we will ever imagine,” he added. item.title: 2027: No rainbow coalition, Plateau is going APC — Mutfwang
item.description: …Declares no vacancy in Aso Rock, Plateau Government House By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has dismissed suggestions of a possible rainbow coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that the state has chosen the All Progressives Congress (APC) as its political platform. Mutfwang also declared that there was no vacancy in Aso Rock and the Plateau State Government House, expressing confidence that President Bola Tinubu and himself would secure re-election in 2027. The governor spoke on Monday while inaugurating the APC presidential and state campaign councils in Plateau State, where he urged party members and campaign officials to intensify mobilisation across the state. “Some people are talking about rainbow, we are talking about a unification movement. Plateau people have decided 2027 to go one direction. “And we have chosen that the wings on which we have chosen to fly in 2027 are the wings of the APC,” he said. Soliciting support for a second term, Mutfwang thanked Plateau residents for their support, insisting that projects and programmes initiated by his administration should be allowed to continue. “We are going to the nooks and crannies of Plateau State to solicit their endorsement and approval for a second time in office because the many things we have begun must not be aborted,” he said. Describing leadership as a relay race, the governor said his administration was determined to build on existing achievements and leave the state better than it met it. On the challenges of hunger and insecurity, Mutfwang acknowledged the difficulties confronting residents but defended his administration’s efforts to address them. He announced plans to strengthen Operation Rainbow and deploy additional forest guards to improve security and facilitate the return of displaced persons to their ancestral communities. “Next week, we are going to commission another batch of retrained Operation Rainbow operatives, and within the next four weeks, we are going to deploy not less than 800 trained forest guards,” he said. Defending President Tinubu’s economic reforms, the governor said the current administration inherited a difficult economic situation from its predecessor, arguing that the reforms were necessary to stabilise the economy. “The President inherited an economy that was tottering on the brink of collapse, and the reforms were necessary to rescue the country,” he said. Highlighting measures introduced by his administration to cushion the impact of economic adjustments on residents, Mutfwang listed the introduction of metro buses, revival of the intra-city rail system, a 50 per cent reduction in tertiary institution fees and increased student allowances. item.title: Vatican names first laywoman to head communications
item.description: The Vatican has appointed 39-year-old Mexican-American media executive, Maria Alvarado, as its new head of communications, making her the first laywoman and first non-Italian to lead the department. Alvarado, who assumes office this week, will oversee the Vatican’s television, radio and print operations, as well as its press office. Her appointment, announced in June by Pope Leo XIV, marks a significant development in the Church’s leadership structure, where senior positions traditionally held by women have largely been occupied by nuns. Alvarado, popularly known as Montse, said her appointment came directly from the Pope rather than through a conventional recruitment process. “I didn’t apply; I wasn’t chosen” through a standard application process, she said in an interview with EWTN News, where she has served as president and chief operating officer since 2023. “It was an appointment from the Holy Father,” she added. EWTN News is the news division of the Eternal Word Television Network, the largest Catholic television network in the United States. Founded by a nun, the network has become an influential platform among conservative Catholics. However, some of its programmes have had a strained relationship with the Vatican, particularly during the papacy of Pope Francis, whose reform agenda attracted criticism from sections of the Church’s conservative wing. In 2021, Francis appeared to criticise the network, lamenting what he described as a major Catholic television channel that was constantly criticising the Pope. Alvarado was a presenter for EWTN at the time. Born in Mexico, Alvarado moved to the United States as a child and grew up in Miami before relocating to Washington for her studies. She spent 14 years working at the Becket Fund for Religious Liberty, a non-profit law firm specialising in the defence of religious freedom, before taking charge of EWTN News in 2023. At EWTN, she oversaw international media platforms producing content in seven languages across television, print, radio, digital media and social networks. Alvarado said she had not originally envisaged a career in media and communications, explaining that her ambition had been to get married and have children. She was previously married, but the marriage was subsequently annulled by the Catholic Church. She succeeds 70-year-old Paolo Ruffini, who was appointed by Pope Francis in 2018 and became the first layperson to head a Vatican dicastery, the Church’s equivalent of a government ministry. Lucetta Scaraffia, founder of the Vatican women’s magazine, Women Church World, and a professor of history at Rome’s La Sapienza University, described Alvarado’s appointment as a recognition of her professional abilities. “This is a woman who has been chosen for her skills and her qualities,” Scaraffia told AFP. item.title: Ebola reminder of urgent need to finish pandemic treaty: WHO chief
item.description: Deadly outbreaks like the Ebola epidemic raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo show the urgent need to complete an international pandemic treaty, the World Health Organization chief said Monday. Wealthy countries and developing nations remain at loggerheads over how an agreement, adopted last year as a framework to handle future Covid-like pandemics, will work in practice. As the ninth meeting towards finalising the deal opened in Geneva Monday, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on countries to “finish the job”. Pointing to several recent deadly disease outbreaks, he stressed that completing a pandemic treaty was “about protecting people”. “A pathogen threat anywhere can become a threat everywhere, to people of every country,” he said, according to a written version of his statement. “The outbreak of hantavirus earlier this year, and the ongoing Ebola epidemic in DRC remind us of this threat.” He was referring to the hantavirus outbreak that killed three people on a cruise ship in April and the latest Ebola outbreak, declared in May, which has killed nearly 5,000 people out of more than 10,000 infected mostly in the DRC. It was vital, Tedros said, that the world learn the overarching lesson of the Covid-19 pandemic: “no country can protect itself from pandemics by acting alone”. When countries agreed in May 2025 to a Pandemic Agreement, they left out the tricky issue of how the key mechanism would operate to get the deal over the line. The agreement’s Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) system covers how to share access to pathogens with pandemic potential, as well as benefits derived from them such as vaccines, tests and treatments. “PABS is the last remaining piece of our puzzle,” Tedros said. During the Covid pandemic, he highlighted that “the world developed vaccines in record time, but too many countries were left waiting while others secured far more than they needed”. “That inequity cost lives, prolonged the pandemic and increased the risk of new variants emerging.” Completing the final piece of the pandemic treaty, he insisted, was “the key that will unlock the door to a safer future”. item.title: Court delivers judgment in alleged terrorism financing case against Tukur Mamu
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday fixed Jan. 27, 2027, for judgment in a charge filed by the Federal Government against Tukur Mamu, alleged terrorists’ negotiator during the Abuja-Kaduna train attack hostages in 2022. Justice Mohammed Umar fixed the date after the Federal Government’s lawyer, David Kaswe, and Mamu’s counsel, Johnson Usman, SAN, adopted their final written addresses and presented their arguments for and against the case. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Mamu, who was arrested on Sept. 7, 2022 by the Egyptian security officials at the Cairo International Airport, was earlier arraigned on a 10-count charge bordering on terrorism financing. However, the prosecution amended the counts by bringing in more offences, including unlawful possession of firearms without valid licence and money laundering charges. When the case was called on Monday, Usman informed the court that the case was scheduled for the adoption of the parties’ final written addresses. The senior lawyer said the defendant’s final written address was dated July 22 but filed July 23. “Our reply on points of law is dated Oct. 30 and filed the same day. “We adopt these two addresses, and we humbly urge this honourable court to graciously acquit and discharge the defendant on all the counts preferred by the Federal Government as the same, having not been proven in any manner,” he prayed. Usman argued that though the defence team had consistently demanded the licence of the rifle allegedly recovered from Mamu’s residence, the lawyer said the prosecution had failed to produce the licence in court. “You mean the expired licence?” Justice Umar asked Usman. Responding, Usman submitted that their contention was that the licence had not expired as of the time Mamu was arrested. He said even though the prosecution took custody of the arms and the licence, their failure to produce the licence in court had raised serious issues of doubt. He, therefore, urged the court to resolve the issue in favour of his client. “My lord, if my vehicle licence expires and my car is parked at home, the VIO cannot arrest me. ”We have asked for this three consecutive times, but they failed to produce it in court,” he said. But Kaswe, as assistant director, who appeared for the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) on behalf of the Federal Government, disagreed with Usman’s submission. The prosecution lawyer recalled that the licence and the rifle had already been tendered before the court. “My Lord, the record of this court will show that we have tendered the licence together with the arms on the day the PW-5, an exhibit keeper, was led on evidence,” he added. Kaswe reminded us that after the prosecution applied for a safekeeping of the rifle and other exhibits, the court granted their request. item.title: PHOTOS: Tinubu granted access to pray inside Ka’abah
item.description: The Custodian of the Holy Mosques of Makkah and Madinah, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, has granted President Bola Ahmed Tinubu a rare privilege of leading Nigeria’s delegation to pray inside the Holy Ka’abah. The president was led into Ka’abah by Sheikh Dahlulah Muthawal of Masjid al-Haram. Tinubu thanked the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud for granting him and members of his Nigerian delegation the opportunity to enter the Holy Ka’abah in Makkah and offer prayers to Almighty Allah. ANA @45: Towards a National Renaissance Sokoto: Concerns over attack on ADC guber candidate’s convoy The President described the honour as a historic and deeply cherished spiritual experience, reflecting the longstanding bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between Nigeria and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. President Tinubu said faith in Allah had strengthened his conviction that his emergence as Nigeria’s leader was an extraordinary blessing that must be matched with dedicated service to the country.
